title: Cross-SDK retry handshake and idempotency compatibility guide
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: This ticket defines a convergent cross-SDK approach for retry/backoff defaults, idempotency key semantics, and streaming handshake behavior across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs. The goal is to reduce cross-language user confusion, prevent accidental duplicate side effects, and provide predictable streaming resume and fallback behavior. Scope includes: named retry presets, full-jitter backoff algorithm, idempotency key generation and header mapping, streaming session handshake and resume token semantics, and a retryable error taxonomy with mapping to HTTP/gRPC/transport errors. Out of scope: server-side policy enforcement, transport-specific kernel optimizations.
decision_record: Adopt three named retry profiles with explicit numeric parameters (fast, balanced, conservative). Use full-jitter backoff. Require/encourage client-supplied idempotency keys for mutating endpoints; SDKs will generate uuidv4 by default when not provided. Streaming handshake will include session-id and resume-token; clients may resume only when server indicates resume-window and provides a valid resume-token. Retryable errors are classified into retryable_transient, retryable_throttling, non_retryable, and stream_resume_possible.
design_notes: Fast: initial=50ms, max=200ms, multiplier=1.5, attempts=3; Balanced: initial=100ms, max=1000ms, multiplier=2.0, attempts=4; Conservative: initial=200ms, max=2000ms, multiplier=2.5, attempts=6. Use full jitter: sleep = random_between(0, cap) where cap grows by multiplier bounded by max. Idempotency key format: uuidv4; SDKs append optional sequence/part suffix for chunked uploads. Header mapping: HTTP header 'Idempotency-Key' recommended; low-level transports include metadata key 'x-redwood-idempotency'. For streaming, initial request header contains 'Requested-Resume=true' optional. Server response contains 'Session-Id' and 'Resume-Token' when resumability is supported. Resume flow: client reopens stream with Session-Id + Resume-Token; server validates token HMAC and respond with resume-offset. Streaming retries are allowed only on transient network errors and server side indicated resumability. Error taxonomy mapping: network timeouts, connection resets => retryable_transient; HTTP 429, 503 => retryable_throttling with backoff cap increase recommendation; 4xx client errors (400/401/403/404) => non_retryable; stream protocol errors with resume-token present => stream_resume_possible.
acceptance_criteria: Python/TS/Go SDKs expose identical named retry presets with matching semantics and unit tests
README and quickstart examples show idempotency usage for create/update and for chunked uploads
Streaming handshake and resume implemented with unit + e2e tests demonstrating resume after network interruption
Telemetry keys emitted for retry_attempts, final_outcome, idempotency_key_present, and resume_attempts
Cross-SDK compatibility tests added to CI to validate header names and session/resume contracts

comments: 2025-02-18 - Aisha Kumar: Created initial proposal after cross-SDK sync; observed three customer incidents where inconsistent client retry semantics caused duplicate resource creation.
2025-02-20 - Daniel Park: Ran tabletop failure injection tests; discovered Python SDK currently uses capped exponential without jitter leading to thundering retry bursts.
2025-02-24 - Priya Singh (SDK PM): Asked for explicit guidance when users override per-request backoff (we should not mutate global presets; expose a per-request override that validates inputs).
2025-02-27 - Security review (notes): Streaming resume tokens must be HMAC-signed by server and TTLed; client SDKs should validate server signature when possible and refuse insecure resumes.
2025-03-01 - Engineering review: Agreed on full jitter and uuidv4 default id keys; flagged server HMAC validation and key rotation as follow-up work for Private deployments.
2025-03-05 - Aisha Kumar: Updated spec to include resume-token HMAC validation recommendation, added migration note for existing clients who relied on legacy backoff values.
release_notes: Introduce cross-sdk retry presets (fast/balanced/conservative), default idempotency-key generation (uuidv4), and streaming resume handshake. Backward-incompatible: SDKs will change default backoff parameters; include migration guide in CHANGELOG.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Changing defaults may increase customer retry counts or alter p99. Mitigation: ship as opt-in flag for first release and enable by default in next minor release; add telemetry to monitor user-visible impact. Risk: resume token security. Mitigation: HMAC tokens, TTL, server rotation and enforce validation in SDKs.
notes_for_release_engineering: Coordinate with runtime team to emit Resume-Token and Session-Id in first rollout. Add guardrail that servers only advertise resumability when storage of partial state is available.
